claim: Explicit forecast-origin availability materially changes estimates of meteorological value
strongest_contradicting_evidence: The external corpus contains operational AQ systems and many meteorological-predictor studies, but no verified result in the audited sources demonstrates that retrospective and origin-available meteorology produce different incremental estimates on identical support.
strongest_supporting_evidence: The P2/P3 availability contract identifies issue time, forecast cycle and latency as information-bearing distinctions; legacy P2 comparisons are retrospective and therefore cannot settle the contrast.
maximum_defensible_position: P3 may test whether the estimated meteorological increment depends on an explicitly defined origin-availability condition; it cannot claim that it does until the comparison is executed.

claim: Retrospective observed/reanalysis meteorology can overestimate operational incremental value
strongest_contradicting_evidence: ERA5/reanalysis and observed-weather studies are commonly used as retrospective covariates, while operational systems such as CAMS/NAQFC use forecast products; the audited sources do not provide a matched empirical overstatement estimate.
strongest_supporting_evidence: The information conditions are technically distinct, and CAMS/ECMWF documentation shows that forecast products have issue and availability schedules that differ from retrospective fields.
maximum_defensible_position: Retrospective meteorology is an upper-bound condition whose relationship to operational value should be tested; no overstatement claim is currently licensed.

claim: The incremental meteorological value changes with forecast horizon
strongest_contradicting_evidence: The Madrid--Ireland/P1-P2 line already evaluates horizon-wise meteorological increments and H*-type horizon summaries; multi-horizon AQ studies also report lead-dependent performance.
strongest_supporting_evidence: The current P3 question could condition horizon effects on forecast-origin availability, but that would be an extension of existing horizon analysis.
maximum_defensible_position: Report any availability-conditioned increment horizon by horizon as a result, not as an independent novelty claim.

claim: Operational meteorology extends baseline-relative predictability compared with lags_only
strongest_contradicting_evidence: The legacy Madrid/Ireland line already reports meteorology-versus-lags comparisons, and CAMS/NAQFC systems establish operational AQ forecasting practice; neither proves the result on the current P3 panel with a provenance-complete predictor stream.
strongest_supporting_evidence: Operational forecast products and schedules exist in ECMWF/CAMS documentation, so a future controlled test is technically conceivable.
maximum_defensible_position: If executed, state only whether the specified operational condition added persistence-relative skill on the evaluated support and horizons.

claim: Error-based meteorological skill gains do not necessarily imply equivalent preservation of pollutant dynamics/events
strongest_contradicting_evidence: P4/P3 diagnostic work already treats skill--fidelity/event disagreement as a high-overlap line; Huang et al. report variability/extreme-event tension and FuXi-Air reports meteorology-linked peak/smoothing consequences.
strongest_supporting_evidence: A future meteorology-condition comparison could show whether the same divergence persists under an operational information contract.
maximum_defensible_position: Use dynamic and event diagnostics as secondary interpretation checks on meteorological gains, not as the primary P3 novelty.
